introHeading: The 3D slider booth for Queens' catering halls and lofts
introParas: Queens catering halls tend to have the kind of open floor Astoria and Flushing weddings need for two hundred guests, and that works in the 3D slider's favor — the motorized track wants roughly 12ft of clear width at normal ceiling height, more room than our other booths ask for, and a big hall gives it space to run without crowding the dance floor. Long Island City's converted loft venues bring the same advantage from a different angle: real ceiling height that a boutique venue elsewhere in the borough might not have.

The format itself is built to stand out in a room that's already seen a lot of photo booths. A camera glides the length of the track past your guests mid-pose, capturing them from multiple angles in a single take — the stitched clip has genuine depth, and it's common for guests to ask to see it replayed before they even step off. That novelty is a strong match for Forest Hills Sweet Sixteens and prom season, where a catering hall floor sees a hundred phones already recording and a familiar photo booth doesn't register the same way. Motion effects, a backdrop chosen with you in advance, and a branded overlay on every clip round it out.

A trained attendant runs the whole rental, sessions are unlimited, and every clip goes out instantly by text, email or QR code with an online gallery afterward. Queens is a standard service area with no surprise fees — travel is quoted from your venue ZIP code before you book — and we're out across Astoria, Long Island City, Flushing, Forest Hills, Jamaica and Ridgewood most weekends.

faqHeading: 3D Slider Photo Booth in Queens — FAQ

faqs.q: Does the 3D slider fit in a Queens catering hall?
faqs.a: Usually with room to spare. Catering halls in Astoria and Flushing tend to have the open floor plan the slider's 12ft track needs, more comfortably than a smaller boutique venue would. Send us your hall's layout and we'll confirm before you book.

faqs.q: Is it a good fit for a prom or Sweet Sixteen?
faqs.a: Yes — it's one of our most requested booths for that crowd. The depth effect is unlike a standard photo booth, and teenagers who've already seen every filter on their phones tend to ask to replay the clip before they even step off the track.

faqs.q: Is there a travel fee for the 3D slider in Queens?
faqs.a: No surprise fees. Queens is a standard service area, and travel is quoted from your venue ZIP code before you book.

faqs.q: How much ceiling height and floor width does the slider need?
faqs.a: Roughly 12ft of clear width at normal ceiling height, more than our other booths ask for. Long Island City loft venues tend to have the height comfortably; we'll confirm the fit for your specific venue before you book.

faqs.q: Do guests need to hold still during the slide?
faqs.a: Only for a few seconds — our attendant cues each group so they know exactly when to hold their pose, and re-runs are unlimited if someone blinks.

faqs.q: Is an attendant included with the rental?
faqs.a: Yes. A trained attendant runs the booth for the full length of your rental, coaching guests through the slide and handling setup and pack-down.

The track takes a bit longer than our smaller booths to set up and test, so we arrive a full hour before your scheduled start. If you need us on site earlier than that, idle time runs at $150 per hour.

faqs.q: Do you carry insurance for Queens venues that require a COI?
faqs.a: Yes. We carry a $3 million liability insurance policy, and catering halls across Astoria and Flushing are used to receiving one — send us their contact details and we'll take care of it.

faqs.q: Would the 3D slider work for a Queens quinceañera?
faqs.a: Yes — it's a strong fit for a quinceañera court specifically, since the depth-effect clip stands out from the standard photo booth every guest has already seen, and the branded overlay can carry the honoree's name and theme colors.

faqs.q: Is parking available for guests near Astoria or Flushing catering halls?
faqs.a: Most of the larger halls in those neighborhoods have their own guest parking lots, which is different from the street parking more common near Long Island City's loft venues.
